prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-05-08. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 12.41 |
| Retained earnings       | 45,912M |
| Current liabilities     | 15,003M |
| Current assets          | 186,246M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 49,234M |
| Total liabilities       | 444,085M |
| Total assets            | 493,319M |
| EBIT / operating income | 3,188M |
| Revenue                 | 7,300M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-05-08, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided metrics indicate a highly leveraged entity (equity only ~10% of total assets; total liabilities/equity ~9x) with minimal scale of operations (EBIT and revenue each <1.5% of assets). This is offset by exceptional liquidity (current ratio of 12.4x, with current assets far exceeding all current liabilities) and a solid equity base that consists almost entirely of retained earnings. These factors together are consistent with a non-investment-grade but not distressed profile on a conventional rating scale.
DECISION: BB
(The rating is assigned purely from the supplied ratios and balance-sheet structure; no external data or forward-looking assumptions are used.)
